title: OKR draft synopsis & rapid decomposition kit — Q2 planning (v0.1)
summary: Working draft to consolidate executive asks, a compact set of candidate OKRs for Q2, and a lightweight decomposition kit to turn each objective into a deliverable sprint slate. Intended as the input doc for the exec alignment session and the all‑hands priority announcement.
background: We need a tighter bridge between founder/exec intent and team-level commitments. Past quarters showed drift between stated objectives and the artifacts teams shipped. This doc proposes a short list of cross-company objectives, each with 2–3 measurable key results and a one-page decomposition pattern teams can adopt quickly.
candidate_objectives: Objective A: Make inference reliably 2x cheaper for tail latency-sensitive workloads
Objective B: Ship Redwood Private GA for regulated customers with audit-grade logging
Objective C: Reduce per-request p95 latency across hosted API by 20%
Objective D: Improve developer onboarding time to first API call from signup to production by 50%
candidate_key_results: Obj A — KR1: Reduce per-token infra cost on 95th percentile workloads by 40% for top 10 enterprise customers
Obj A — KR2: Deploy intelligent prefix caching to 30% of production routes and measure 15% average token savings
Obj B — KR1: Complete SOC‑2 readiness checklist and run 2 customer audits in private deployments
Obj B — KR2: Deliver VPC/gateway pattern with KMS integration and documented runbook
Obj C — KR1: Reach p95 <= 200ms for single-turn generation on standard beta models for hosted tier
Obj D — KR1: Launch templates + CLI quickstart and measure median time-to-first-successful-call <= 10 minutes
decomposition_kit_instructions: Use this rapid template to turn an objective into a 6‑week sprint: 1) Define top‑level metric and current baseline. 2) List the three smallest experiments that could move that metric (measure, iterate, rollback). 3) Assign owner + 2 cross-functional partners. 4) State deployment and rollback criteria. 5) Capture instrumentation plan (dashboards, alerts). Keep each item to one paragraph.
example_decomposition_for_obj_a: Baseline: per-token cost measured at $0.0009 median and $0.0025 95th for sampled enterprise routes. Experiment 1: aggressive KV caching for repeated user prefixes (owner: Miguel, infra partner: Leah) — metric: tokens saved per session; rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with canary. Experiment 2: runtime kernel selection policy that prefers lower-precision quantized kernels for non-critical routes. Experiment 3: request routing policy to fall back to cheaper model variants under heavy load. Each experiment should include a hypothesis line and the success threshold before scaling.
run_of_show_for_exec_alignment_session: 0–10m: context & goals (CEO) — why these objectives matter
10–25m: walk candidate objectives and KRs (Asha) — key tradeoffs
25–40m: breakout by theme (cost, reliability, product velocity) — rapid feedback
40–55m: decision framing and ratification (execs) — pick top 2 cross-company objectives
allhands_communication_outline: Headliner slide: two company objectives + 3 company-level asks for individual contributors. Follow with 3 short stories showing what success looks like (cost saved, customer onboarded to Private, faster onboarding). Provide links to team templates and decomposition kit and call out where to drop feedback (Slack #q2-okr-feedback).
roles_and_owners: Program lead: Asha Patel — coordinate exec alignment & all-hands comms
Cost pillar lead: Miguel Torres — cost experiments, infra gating
Private & Compliance lead: Sanjay Rao — private GA workstreams and audits
Developer Experience lead: Leah Kim — quickstarts, templates, onboarding metrics
major_risks: Risk: Overcommitting to 4+ cross-company objectives -> dilution. Mitigation: execs pick max 2 cross-company objectives, others become team-owned targets.
Risk: Instrumentation lag hides regressions. Mitigation: mandate dashboards for each KR before any rollout beyond canary.
Risk: Customer-impacting regressions from aggressive quantization. Mitigation: define per-route safety flags and automatic rollback thresholds.
decision_points_needed_from_execs: Confirm top 2 cross-company objectives to cascade
Approve experimental guardrails for runtime quantization (safety thresholds)
Allocate 4 FTE-equivalent for the inaugural Private GA support window
timeline: Week 0: exec alignment session; Week 1–2: teams adopt decomposition kit and post sprint slates; Week 3–8: run experiments + canaries; Week 9: cross-company review & metric readout; Week 10: prepare all‑hands announcement and customer comms.
measurement_and_reporting: Weekly metric digest published to /company/metrics with a short one‑paragraph update from each pillar lead. Ops will maintain a live decision log capturing rollouts, regressions, and mitigation actions.
next_steps: Finalize candidate objectives after exec session (owner: Asha) — due +3 business days
Create per-objective quickstart template in GitHub (owner: Leah) — due +7 days
Schedule canary cohorts and instrumentation checkpoints (owner: Miguel) — due +10 days
open_questions: What minimum SLA must Private GA meet to be considered 'production ready'?
What is the gating rubric for deciding a model-variant fallback vs. preserving model fidelity?
How do we credit cross-team contributions when multiple teams affect the same KR metric?
notes_to_reviewers: This is intentionally concise — please annotate copied sections with GitHub PR comments or drop quick reactions in #q2-okr-feedback. If you disagree with an objective, propose an alternative objective + one measurable KR and a short rationale.
